A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Instruct-4DGS work, including the complete main text, references, and three supplementary pages. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v2 reports original editing-quality and runtime experiments in Tables 1–2, a 50-participant preference study in Figure 8, and supplementary qualitative results in Figures 9–11.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative experiments, 50-participant preference study, and supplementary qualitative results reported in v2.

M1.justification: Sections 4 and 7.1 retain the same static Gaussian editing, Coherent-IP2P score-based refinement, and monocular adaptation that skips Stage 1. No algorithm, component, or loss changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate DyNeRF and Technicolor multiview scenes, DyCheck and HyperNeRF monocular scenes, and varying-camera-pose rendering. Dataset and task coverage in Sections 5 and 7 is identical.

E2.justification: Instruct 4D-to-4D remains the comparator in Tables 1–2 and Figures 6–7 and 9. The four method variants compared in Figure 8 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The 50-frame evaluation segments, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/CLIP metrics, guidance scales, iteration budgets, GPU settings, and 50-participant preference-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 8 retains the same analyses of fully SDS-based editing, original-IP2P refinement, and deformation-field refinement. The temporal-refinement demonstration and supplementary viewpoint-consistency analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and user-preference proportions. Neither provides additional repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 retains average LPIPS values of 0.303 for Instruct-4DGS and 0.491 for I4D24D; Table 2 retains 40 minutes on one GPU and 2 hours on two GPUs, respectively.

T1.justification: The Gaussian and Hexplane definitions and mathematical formulations, including Equations (1)–(2), are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning static-component editing, score-based temporal refinement, reduced editing time, and improved visual quality.

C2.justification: The explanations of temporal misalignment and perceptual versus pixel-level quality are identical. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning IP2P dependence, motion editing, segmentation for partial edits, and residual motion artifacts.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page hyperlink labeled 'Code and results' to the abstract, providing access information absent from v2. Implementation details and supplementary editing instructions remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked resources.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and 70-reference bibliography are unchanged. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a short code/results pointer, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All remaining prose and the organization of the main text and supplementary material are unchanged.

P2.justification: The hyperlink causes minor abstract reflow and spacing changes on page 1. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–2 are unchanged, and pages 2–14 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new 'Code and results' pointer provides a small improvement in resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged, and the supplied PDFs do not establish the availability or completeness of the linked resources.
